prompt: A magazine cross-number puzzle, shown completely solved. It is a 3 by 3 grid of single-digit cells; each row read left to right is a 3-digit number (the ACROSS answers) and each column read top to bottom is a 3-digit number (the DOWN answers), and no answer may start with 0. The printed clues are: 1 ACROSS (top row) is a three-digit prime number; 2 ACROSS (middle row) is a multiple of 111; 3 ACROSS (bottom row) is a palindrome (reads the same forwards and backwards); 1 DOWN (left column) is a multiple of 9; 3 DOWN (right column) is a three-digit prime; and 2 DOWN (middle column) equals the 1 ACROSS number minus the 3 ACROSS number. Exactly one filling of the grid satisfies every clue at once. Draw the fully solved grid with one digit centred in each of the nine cells so all six clues hold; add no other writing beyond the grid.
